items.title: Does SHL Record Your Screen? Webcam, Window Switching, and Remote Proctoring Rules
items.pt:
You are about to start an SHL assessment when the browser asks for camera access, microphone permission, or full-screen mode. The natural reaction is: Does SHL record my screen, and will switching windows get me flagged?

The accurate answer is more nuanced than a simple yes or no. SHL can monitor webcam, microphone, and screen activity when the employer enables proctoring, but not every SHL assessment records a continuous video of your desktop. Some configurations log browser focus, screenshot

items.title: Bi-FORK: Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Bifurcating Systems
items.pt: Bifurcations are ubiquitous in physical systems, from structural buckling to fluid and climate dynamics, yet they remain largely unexplored in deep learning. At a symmetry-breaking bifurcation, a single input admits multiple equally valid solutions, violating the one-to-one assumption underlying most learned physical surrogates. items.title: Caught in the Act: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
items.pt: Recent incidents have highlighted the challenge of monitoring LLM agents and the danger of models deceiving people. We show that white-box deception detection via probes can be scaled up to frontier monitoring settings by collecting the largest deception dataset to date for training probes and introducing a novel probe architecture which can aggregate information across many layers and tokens. items.title: WorldGuide: Goal-Directed Video World Model for Procedural Task Execution
items.pt: Video generators and video-based world models can synthesize plausible visual trajectories, but long-horizon procedural tasks require generation to adapt to what has actually been produced. items.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
items.pt: We propose BrickBench, a benchmark for agentic text-conditioned LEGO-set design. Given a prompt, an agent is tasked with producing an assembly that not only satisfies semantic and design criteria, but that can also be physically built. To do so, it must select parts from a discrete library and reason jointly about local and global constraints. We score validity, alignment, and design across three settings that vary in scale and part availability. We provide BrickAgent, an environment for coding
